means:
Giving a **broad general view of a whole subject at once** — everything laid out together, seen from above.

A synoptic account isn't merely a *short* one. **Summary** means shortened; **synoptic** means *wide* — all the parts visible in relation to each other. The word is formal and faintly technical (meteorologists, theologians, planners, strategists use it straight), and it's quietly approving: breadth achieved, altitude gained. Nobody calls a rambling overview synoptic.
trap: ⚠️ **synoptic ≠ synaptic.** *Synaptic* belongs to the **synapse** — the gap between nerve cells. One is a wide view; the other is a tiny junction in your brain.
trick_line: **Syn-OPTIC** hides **OPTIC** — it's the wide-angle lens, not the zoom.
trick_unpack: You get the whole scene in a single frame, which is exactly why a synoptic view buys breadth and gives up fine detail.
sentences: The commission's report opens with a **synoptic** chapter placing three decades of policy failure on a single page.
Skip the deep dive for now — just give me the **synoptic** version before the meeting starts.
in_the_wild: Matthew, Mark and Luke are called the **Synoptic Gospels** — they can be set side by side in parallel columns and read *together*, because they share one broad view of events. John, which doesn't line up, is excluded.
etymology:
Greek **syn-** (*together*) + **opsis** (*sight, view*) — "seeing it all together."

*Opsis* is a workhorse root: **synopsis** (the view-together), **optic** (of sight), **autopsy** (*auto-* + *opsis* = seeing for oneself), **myopia** (short sight), **biopsy** (viewing living tissue).
one_line: Giving a broad overview of the whole at once.
